## Outcome
Cost is a function of the answer, not the archive. The same binary serves a three-item scratch project created minutes ago and a million-item workspace spanning decades, with no special mode the agent has to know about.

## Why this is a milestone, not an epic
pm-9rxu is the living execution epic. This milestone is the outcome gate: it declares the scale claims the GA contract is allowed to publish.

## Delivery chain
pm-801d persistent derived read index -> pm-plwm index-backed --where predicates -> pm-0qg5 item-directory fan-out -> pm-lvyd claim throughput -> pm-o79o growth policy -> pm-5qmm memory tiers for decades-old epochs. Spectrum stories pm-g2zz (large) and pm-z436 (small) are the acceptance narratives.

## Explicit non-goals
No daemon (ADR pm-i7i4). No external database requirement for the base install. No scale mode the agent has to opt into.
Outcome milestone: proven scale — sub-second bounded-token context at a million items with thousands of concurrent agents

list/context/next/get-by-filter are served from a derived index with cost proportional to the result, not the workspace; Published benchmark evidence at 1M items shows sub-second bounded-token context assembly on commodity hardware; Claim and lock throughput is measured under thousands of concurrent agents with documented contention behaviour; The small end is proven too: a three-item scratch workspace pays proportional, near-zero ceremony and token cost; History and repository growth stay bounded by an automated compaction, gc, and archival policy
Context assembly cost is bounded by the answer size, not the workspace size, at every scale from three items to a million
Scale is the claim that distinguishes pm from a flat-file backlog: an agent must not pay for workspace size it never reads.
Determines whether pm can host decade-spanning, multi-team, thousands-of-agents workspaces or stays a single-repo tool.
Published, reproducible benchmark evidence for latency, memory, token cost, and claim throughput at the million-item and thousand-agent points.
The read path still scans item files; every capability added before the index lands inherits the scan and has to be re-tuned afterwards.
